rv.q: In this case, more is unsurprisingly less.
Blue Man Group's interactive holiday pleasures aren’t evenly distributed in a large Broadway venue.

They also happen to be excellent percussionists. If you were a fan when you first saw them downtown, you’ll know just what to expect. Despite its subtitle – A New Holiday Surprise – there’s really not much to be surprised about in this comeback.
Call me Scrooge, but by the time “Blue Man Group: A New Holiday Surprise” ended with a typically over-the-top finale, drawing wild applause and cheers, I was more than ready to leave.
But while the 90 minutes are stuffed with well-executed stunt and spectacle, too much of the show feels random, dated, underdeveloped, or almost perfunctory.
There is nothing original, festive, or surprising about this “New Holiday Surprise” at the Lunt-Fontanne.

As directed by Matt Ramsey , Blue Man Group's A New Holiday Surprise is a kaleidoscope of sight and sound that often resembles what might happen if three aliens landed on Earth and tried to figure out Christmas.

If you've ever spent an evening with Blue Man Group, this is a regift in shinier paper, but anyone looking for low-hanging mistletoe or with a tiny tot in tow will find it a merry, marshmallow-pelted good time.

cn.t: Critics find Blue Man Group's Broadway holiday debut more familiar than fresh — the signature blue antics are intact, but the "surprise" feels thin, with most reviewers noting a lack of originality or genuine festive spirit.

sg.ra: Closest and most direct view of the stage at Lunt-Fontanne Theatre, with the fullest sound. The standard top pick for any show here.
An elevated, full-stage view with no orchestra-level neck-craning — especially strong for shows with big staging or choreography.
A modest side angle on the stage but still close and clear — a reliable choice when center seats are sold out.
Farther from the stage than center orchestra — less up-close, but the sound still carries well.
A noticeable side angle, but Lunt-Fontanne Theatre's more moderate size keeps the distance from the stage manageable.

vs.sum: A handsome Art Deco house with a distinctive celestial ceiling and wide auditorium. Sightlines are good from center seats but the wide layout means far-side seats lose some stage width. Notoriously narrow seats make comfort a challenge for longer shows.

acc.note: Step-free to lobby and Orchestra. Copper induction loop available. 5 wheelchair spaces.
